body:
A second full local run produced a DIFFERENT failure set from the first, which rules out the
order-dependence this finding originally hypothesised.

- run 1 (quiet machine, 315s): 1 failed / 5924 passed --
  `test_1094_...::TestConversionDeadline::test_convert_book_passes_the_deadline_to_the_converter`
- run 2 (loaded machine, 152s): 6 failed / 5920 passed -- a DIFFERENT set, including
  `test_1094_...::TestFailedConversionStillImports::test_ignored_format_is_imported_exactly_once`,
  `test_1094_...::TestNotABookFormatsAreNotRescued::test_acsm_conversion_failure_does_not_import_the_ticket`,
  and `test_802_metadata_change_dispatch.py::test_enforcer_missing_log_logs_single_info_not_warning_spam`

Pytest here is serial with no randomiser, so a deterministic ORDER problem would reproduce the same
set every time. It does not. Both files pass in isolation (61 passed) and CI's Fast Tests is green
on the same commits.

Sharper hypothesis: these are WALL-CLOCK-SENSITIVE tests -- the failing names are about conversion
deadlines, timeout budgets and subprocess arithmetic -- and they fail when the machine is loaded, not
when the order changes. That also explains why the loaded run was FASTER overall (152s vs 315s):
different contention, not different sequencing.

Still not root-caused, and deliberately not asserted as fact. What would settle it: run the two files
under artificial CPU load with no other change. If they fail, it is timing and the fix is to remove
real clocks from the assertions (freeze/inject time) rather than to hunt a polluting neighbour.

Consequence if ignored: a suite that reds intermittently on a developer machine while CI stays green
gets written off as "just flaky", and a real regression later hides inside that noise
(red-suite-wedges-every-tick).

Superseded note: the original text here blamed order or ambient state and flagged that an explicit
multi-file `pytest f1.py ... f7.py` invocation returned `collected 0 items`. That collection oddity
was not reproduced on retry with two files and should be treated as unconfirmed.
title: Deadline/timeout unit tests fail under full-suite load, never in CI
